modelPurpose: Represents how a cafe app turns a paid order into prepared food for pickup while separating payment correctness from real-world preparation.

product.name: Cafe Ordering App
product.description: A product that lets customers order food and drinks for pickup from a cafe.

lexicon.definition: A world-anchored obligation or capability the product must support, expressed as the KR title.
examples: Reserve an available book copy for pickup
Prepare a paid cafe order for customer pickup
Return an eligible delivered item and issue the correct refund

lexicon.definition: The canonical end-to-end path that fulfills one primary duty, expressed as the KR description.
examples: A member searches for a book, reserves a copy, and receives pickup details.

lexicon.definition: An atomic behavioral transition with preconditions, trigger, and observable postconditions.
examples: Given a copy is available, when a member reserves it, then one active hold is created.

lexicon.definition: A measurable indicator of user-experienced quality, such as latency, correctness, freshness, or recoverability.
A threshold target for a UX SLI that defines acceptable experience for a critical duty or journey.
examples: 99% of valid reservations confirm in under one second.

lexicon.definition: A concrete end-to-end execution example that demonstrates correct behavior for a duty journey.
examples: Successful reservation of one available library copy.

lexicon.definition: A concrete execution example that demonstrates forbidden, failed, misleading, or unacceptable behavior.
examples: Two members receive confirmation for the same physical copy.

lexicon.definition: A domain entity that exists or is meaningful in the real world and anchors the product architecture.
An architectural separation justified by real-world duration, externality, or human/physical delay.
examples: Kitchen preparation may be asynchronous because cooking takes real-world time.

lexicon.definition: A product law that must remain true across all valid states and transitions.
examples: One accepted return may issue at most one refund.

ambiguityPolicy.principle: The model must be internally decidable. If ambiguity remains, the model must name the missing external fact instead of hiding uncertainty in vague wording.
requiresClarificationWhen: A duty cannot be mapped to at least one real-world object or interaction.
A network boundary lacks a real-world latency or causality justification.
A trace can be interpreted as both golden and anti-golden.
A weakening or breaking update lacks explicit compatibility classification.
A journey completion criterion cannot be evaluated from observable state.

objects.name: Customer
objects.definition: A person placing and picking up a cafe order.

objects.name: Cart
objects.definition: A temporary collection of available menu items before checkout.

objects.name: Payment Authorization
objects.definition: A payment decision that approves or declines the order amount.

objects.name: Paid Order
objects.definition: An order that exists after payment acceptance.

objects.name: Kitchen Ticket
objects.definition: The kitchen-facing instruction to prepare the paid order.

interactions.name: Checkout cart
interactions.description: The customer submits cart and payment for order creation.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Checkout is digital but external payment can take seconds.

interactions.name: Prepare food
interactions.description: Kitchen staff prepare the paid order in the real world.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Food preparation takes real-world time and can be asynchronous.

invariants.name: No kitchen ticket without payment
invariants.statement: A kitchen ticket must not be created unless payment is accepted.
invariants.rationale: The kitchen should not prepare unpaid orders accidentally.

networkBoundaries.name: Checkout and payment boundary
networkBoundaries.description: Payment acceptance and paid order creation must be causally linked.
networkBoundaries.realWorldProcess: A customer exchanges payment authorization for a cafe order obligation.
networkBoundaries.causalityJustification: The order must not be sent to the kitchen unless payment acceptance and order creation are causally connected.
networkBoundaries.userVisibleImpact: The customer receives confirmation or payment failure.
networkBoundaries.failureMode: An unpaid kitchen ticket may be created.

networkBoundaries.name: Kitchen preparation boundary
networkBoundaries.description: Kitchen preparation may progress asynchronously after a paid order exists.
networkBoundaries.realWorldProcess: Kitchen staff prepare food and drinks over minutes.
networkBoundaries.causalityJustification: Cooking is physically delayed and can safely proceed asynchronously after payment.
networkBoundaries.userVisibleImpact: The customer sees preparing and ready states.
networkBoundaries.failureMode: A lost ticket leaves a paid order without preparation.

objectives.title: Make pickup orders fast and accurate
objectives.description: Customers can pay for available items and receive reliable preparation status.
objectives.successMeaning: Paid orders reach the kitchen exactly once and customers can trust ready status.

duties.title: Prepare a paid cafe order for customer pickup
duties.intent: Transform a paid cart into food prepared for pickup.
duties.scope: Covers checkout, payment acceptance, kitchen ticket creation, preparation status, and ready notification.

okrMapping.keyResultTitle: Prepare a paid cafe order for customer pickup
okrMapping.keyResultDescription: A customer pays for items, the kitchen prepares them, and the customer sees ready status.

journeys.title: Order cafe items for pickup
journeys.description: A customer checks out a cart, payment is accepted, a kitchen ticket is created, and the order becomes ready for pickup.
journeys.purpose: Bridge digital payment with real-world food preparation.
variants: Order may remain preparing for several minutes.
failureBoundaries: If payment fails, no kitchen ticket is created.
nonGoals: In-store table service is outside this journey.

timing.causalJustification: Checkout requires digital consistency; food preparation takes real-world time and may be asynchronous.

flow.notes: Linear primary flow derived from step order.

steps.title: Checkout cart
steps.then: The system requests payment authorization and shows a resolving state.

stateTransitions.notes: The cart is submitted for checkout.
A payment attempt is initiated (still pending until authorization).

steps.title: Create paid order
steps.then: The system creates a paid order.

stateTransitions.notes: A paid order is created after payment acceptance.

steps.title: Create kitchen ticket
steps.when: The order is accepted for preparation.
steps.then: The system creates exactly one kitchen ticket.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees the order was received by the cafe.

stateTransitions.notes: The paid order is sent to the kitchen.
A kitchen ticket is created for preparation.

steps.title: Mark ready
steps.given: Kitchen staff have prepared the order.
steps.then: The order status changes to ready.
thenAssertions: Ready state is visible to the customer.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees ready for pickup.

steps.title: Reject failed payment
steps.then: The system does not create a paid order or kitchen ticket.
thenAssertions: No kitchen ticket exists after failed payment.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The customer sees payment failure and can retry.

stateTransitions.notes: No paid order is created when payment fails.
No kitchen ticket is created when payment fails.

slis.name: Checkout confirmation time
slis.description: Time from checkout submission to confirmation or clear failure.

slis.name: Kitchen ticket creation reliability
slis.description: Percentage of paid orders that create exactly one kitchen ticket.

slos.name: Checkout resolves under three seconds
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Customers may retry payment or distrust the order state.

slos.name: Kitchen ticket exists for paid orders
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Paid customer orders may not reach the kitchen.

golden.title: Successful cafe pickup order
golden.description: A customer pays successfully and the kitchen prepares the order.
golden.scenario: Cafe is open and cart items are available.
golden.finalState: Paid order is ready for pickup.
golden.classificationReason: The trace satisfies payment-before-preparation and ready-state behavior.

antiGolden.title: Unpaid order sent to kitchen
antiGolden.description: A declined payment still creates a kitchen ticket.
antiGolden.trigger: Customer submits checkout with invalid payment.
antiGolden.finalState: A kitchen ticket exists without payment.

updates.summary: Initial model for preparing paid cafe pickup orders.
updates.reason: Establishes the first complete version of this product representation.
updates.rolloutPlan: Adopt as baseline after schema and semantic validation.
